digest.component_or_area: reconciler transport typing and mypy enforcement
propositions: Reconciler core modules pass transport parameters without type annotations or with Any, preventing mypy from enforcing port completeness.

Absolute imports via the sys.path-injected rebar_reconciler name cause mypy to widen TicketTransport annotations to Any under ignore_missing_imports=true, making annotations silently unenforceable even when present.

Relative imports of TicketTransport within the reconciler package restore mypy's enforcement of port member access, enabling detection of undeclared capability members like add_comment and set_relationship.

Capability members (add_comment, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map) are carried as metaclass attributes so hasattr returns True while mypy protocol checking does not see them, creating a gap the AST audit cannot detect but mypy can via narrowed views.

The _TransportPortMeta metaclass is load-bearing for runtime isinstance conformance checking (preventing ABCMeta subclass cache false positives) and is orthogonal to static typing; splitting it is not required.

Annotating all 38 port parameters in 14 core modules as TicketTransport (imported relatively) with narrowing to composed capability Protocols where needed resolves all mypy enforcement gaps while leaving the runtime guard unchanged.
